title: One turn, end to end
summary: Three processes: the Angular app in the browser, its SSR server (Express, :4200 in dev, :4000 built) and the agent (:10002). The browser speaks plain JSON and SSE to its own server; only the server speaks A2A to the agent; only the agent talks to the model. Read the columns left to right, the numbered steps top to bottom. Open a walk on the right for one complete path.

nodes.label: 1 Prompt or click
nodes.detail: The user asks, or clicks a button on a surface. A click is turned into an A2uiClientAction locally; nothing executes.

nodes.label: 2 POST /a2a
nodes.detail: Same-origin JSON: { query | event | error, sessionId }. The browser never talks to the agent and holds no A2A types or keys.
nodes.payload: { "query": "Show me the open tickets", "sessionId": "<from the last reply>" }

nodes.label: 3 A2A message/stream
nodes.detail: The server wraps the request in one A2A message (text part, or data part { version, action | error }), sets contextId = sessionId and metadata.a2uiClientCapabilities with the ticket catalog id, and calls the agent over JSON-RPC.

nodes.label: 4 Negotiate + read
nodes.detail: pickA2ui picks v0.9 and the ticket catalog from the metadata; readInboundMessage gets text, action or client error; the system prompt is built from that catalog's toJson() and examples.

nodes.label: 5 Build the query
nodes.detail: Text as is; open_ticket prefetches the ticket; a VALIDATION_FAILED redoes the last turn with the error first (once).

nodes.label: 6 Model writes A2UI
nodes.detail: Live: Gemini call 1 asks for get_tickets, the agent runs it (assets/tickets.json, internal_notes included), call 2 streams A2UI v0.9 JSON in <a2ui-json> blocks. Stub: a canned reply in chunks.

nodes.label: 7 Validate as it streams
nodes.detail: Each growing message is checked against the catalog's Zod in a fresh renderer state before it may leave; partial messages wait. A rejected message → retry once with the error, then a text apology.

nodes.label: 8 Policy on every message
nodes.detail: enforcePolicy strips internal_notes and removes Delete (and anything bound to the notes) from every batch, each re-send included, before publishing.

nodes.label: 9 A2A status updates
nodes.detail: working → working + data parts (one A2UI message each, application/a2ui+json) → final input-required (or completed). Text parts carry the fallback.

nodes.label: 10 Unwrap to SSE
nodes.detail: Takes the A2UI messages out of the A2A parts and writes data: { messages, text?, sessionId } per event. No A2A reaches the browser.

nodes.label: 11 Render
nodes.detail: handleEvent stores the sessionId, applies each message: createSurface → updateComponents (validated again, same Zod objects) → updateDataModel; bindings resolve; the Angular catalog components draw the tickets.

nodes.label: 12 Renderer checks values
nodes.detail: Phase 6: what web_core can't see, a bound value outside the schema (priority "critical" in the data model), PriorityBadge catches after resolving it; rejected components become placeholders.

nodes.label: 13 VALIDATION_FAILED back
nodes.detail: After the reply has rendered, at most 2 reports per user turn go back through the same POST /a2a as { error }. The agent redoes the turn once; a second report gets the text fallback.

nodes.label: sessionId = contextId
nodes.detail: The one place the two names meet: the browser keeps an opaque sessionId, the server passes it as A2A contextId, the agent keys its Gemini chat and its client-retry memory by it.

paths.label: "Show me the open tickets"
paths.note: One turn across the three processes.

paths.label: Click Open on a row
paths.note: The action round trip; the ticket is prefetched.

paths.label: The agent rejects its own reply
paths.note: Fixed before anything leaves the agent.

paths.label: The renderer rejects a value (stages 5–6)
paths.note: VALIDATION_FAILED goes back, the agent redoes the turn.

title: In the browser
summary: What happens inside the Angular app: AgentClient sends and reads, the @a2ui/angular renderer (web_core underneath) applies A2UI messages to surfaces and validates components, the catalog components draw them and, in phase 6, check the values their bindings resolve to. Nothing the agent sends is executed.

nodes.label: Prompt form
nodes.detail: The user types a request (default "Show me the open tickets") and submits. app.ts calls AgentClient.ask(prompt). The input and button are disabled while isLoading() is true.

nodes.label: Status lines
nodes.detail: Three signals from AgentClient drive what the user sees besides the UI: waitingForUi() shows "Agent is working…", agentText() shows the agent's text-only answer (the fallback), error() shows a failed request.

nodes.label: Surface list
nodes.detail: app.ts loops over renderer.surfaceGroup.surfacesMap and draws one <a2ui-v09-surface [surfaceId]> per surface. Tracked by the SurfaceModel object, not its id, so a surface deleted and re-created under the same id is drawn afresh (incident 6).

nodes.label: ask(query) / handleAction(event)
nodes.detail: The two ways a turn starts: a prompt, or a button action (the renderer calls handleAction through the actionHandler in app.config.ts). Both reset the report counter and call send().

nodes.label: send(): clear, reset
nodes.detail: Before the request: deletes every surface (each reply carries its whole UI, createSurface included), clears ValidationIssues, sets isLoading and waitingForUi, clears error and agentText. Exception: an error report keeps the old surfaces on screen until the corrected reply's first messages arrive.

nodes.label: POST /a2a
nodes.detail: One fetch to the app's own server, same origin. The body carries exactly one of query, event or error, plus the session id from the previous reply (absent on the first turn).

nodes.label: Read the SSE stream
nodes.detail: The response body is read as text, split on blank lines; each "data: " line is parsed as JSON and passed to handleEvent. A non-200 response throws its { error } into the error signal.
nodes.payload:
data: {"messages":[…A2UI v0.9 messages…],"text":"…","sessionId":"<contextId>"}

data: {"error":"…"}   (only if the stream fails after it started)

nodes.label: handleEvent()
nodes.detail: Per event: an error field throws; sessionId is stored for the next request; text goes to agentText; for each createSurface whose id already exists, that surface is deleted first (a retried reply starts over); then each message goes to process() one at a time, and waitingForUi turns off.

nodes.label: process(message)
nodes.detail: Everything except updateComponents goes straight to the renderer. An updateComponents is tried whole; if web_core throws A2uiValidationError, each component is applied on its own and every rejected one is replaced by a placeholder Text with the same id ("⚠ This part of the answer could not be shown."), and filed in ValidationIssues with path /components/<index>/<prop>.

nodes.label: reportIssues()
nodes.detail: After the stream ends: waits for appRef.whenStable() (components have resolved their bindings), takes the first open issue, and if fewer than 2 reports were sent since the user's last prompt or action, calls send({ error }) with a v0.9 VALIDATION_FAILED. The message counts any other issues ("and N more like it").

nodes.label: A2uiRendererService.processMessages
nodes.detail: The library's entry point. Applies A2UI v0.9 messages to its SurfaceGroup. Registered in app.config.ts with provideA2Ui({ catalogs: [ticket catalog, BasicCatalog], actionHandler }).

nodes.label: createSurface
nodes.detail: Creates a SurfaceModel for surfaceId, bound to the catalog named by catalogId (the ticket catalog). Throws if the id already exists, which is why AgentClient deletes it first.

nodes.label: updateComponents → validate
nodes.detail: Validates every component against the surface catalog's Zod schema (the same ComponentApi objects the agent uses, from packages/catalog). One invalid component rejects the whole message with A2uiValidationError; it never looks at the values bindings resolve to.

nodes.label: updateDataModel → data model
nodes.detail: Writes value at path in the surface's local data model. Components re-read the paths they bind. Typing into an input also writes here, and sends nothing to the agent.

nodes.label: Bindings resolve
nodes.detail: A prop like { "path": "priority" } is read from the data model. Inside a template row the path is relative to the row (/tickets/0), so it resolves /tickets/0/priority. Each catalog component reads it through props().<name>.value().

nodes.label: Button click → action
nodes.detail: A Button's action.event.context paths are resolved against the data model at click time, and the renderer calls the actionHandler with an A2uiClientAction. Nothing runs locally: the action only goes back to the agent.

nodes.label: TicketList
nodes.detail: Draws the title and one row per child; the children come from the template over /tickets, each row a component host with its own data context.

nodes.label: PriorityBadge
nodes.detail: Typed from PriorityBadgeApi (priority: low | medium | high | urgent). After resolving a bound priority it checks the value with resolvedValueProblem(); a value outside the enum shows a dashed "?" and files an issue under surface#component@dataContextPath; a valid value withdraws it.

nodes.label: resolvedValueProblem()
nodes.detail: Phase 6: checks a resolved bound value against the catalog's own Zod for that prop (the value branch of the union only). Returns the absolute data-model path and a message, or null.

nodes.label: AssigneeChip, basic components
nodes.detail: AssigneeChip draws initials + name ("Unassigned" when empty). Text, Row, Column, Card, Divider and Button are the library's own Angular components, limited to the ones the ticket catalog lists.

nodes.label: ValidationIssues
nodes.detail: A map of open problems for the current reply, keyed by whoever found them (AgentClient for a rejected component, PriorityBadge for a bad bound value). Cleared at every send(); read by reportIssues().
nodes.payload: { surfaceId: string, path: string /* JSON pointer */, message: string }

paths.label: A prompt, start to screen
paths.note: From the form to a drawn ticket list.

paths.label: A button action
paths.note: Open on a row: the context is resolved locally, then the turn starts over.

paths.label: A component web_core rejects
paths.note: Placeholder for the bad one, the rest renders, the problem is filed.

paths.label: A bad bound value (stage 5–6)
paths.note: Valid component, invalid value: only the renderer can see it.

title: SSR server and agent
summary: The SSR server is a bridge, not a page renderer here (every route is RenderMode.Client): it turns the browser's POST into an A2A message and the agent's A2A events into SSE. The agent negotiates the catalog, builds the query, asks the model, validates every streamed message against the Zod catalog, applies the server-side policy and publishes A2A status updates.

nodes.label: POST /a2a
nodes.detail: The Express route the browser calls. Reads { query, event, error, sessionId }. A malformed error (missing string code, surfaceId, message, or path for VALIDATION_FAILED) gets 400 and goes no further.

nodes.label: Build the A2A message
nodes.detail: Exactly one part: event → data part { version, action }; error → data part { version, error }; otherwise a text part with the query. The browser's sessionId becomes A2A contextId. The catalogs the app can draw go in metadata: capability negotiation, ids only.

nodes.label: getAgent(): agent card
nodes.detail: On first use: GET <AGENT_URL>/.well-known/agent-card.json (AGENT_URL defaults to http://localhost:10002). The A2AClient is cached; a failed lookup is not (PR #9), so the next request tries again. Every request to the agent carries the header X-A2A-Extensions: https://a2ui.org/a2a-extension/a2ui/v0.9.

nodes.label: sendMessageStream
nodes.detail: A2A JSON-RPC message/stream to the URL in the agent card (http://localhost:10002/a2a/json-rpc). The answer is a stream of A2A events.

nodes.label: Unwrap A2A events
nodes.detail: For each event: task and status-update → status.message.parts; artifact-update → artifact.parts. Data parts are the A2UI messages; text parts are joined into text. The only file that knows A2A: swapping the transport means rewriting this one.

nodes.label: Write SSE to the browser
nodes.detail: Headers text/event-stream, no-cache, keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no. One line per A2A event that has messages, text or a contextId (in practice every event). Errors: before the first byte → 502 { error }; after → data: { error } and end.
nodes.payload:
data: {"messages":[{ "version":"v0.9","createSurface":{…} }, …],"sessionId":"<contextId>"}

data: {"messages":[],"text":"I'm sorry, I'm having trouble…","sessionId":"…"}

nodes.label: Agent HTTP server :10002
nodes.detail: Express app: CORS for http://localhost:* (left from the sample's browser client), GET /.well-known/agent-card.json, POST /a2a/json-rpc. No authentication (UserBuilder.noAuthentication).

nodes.label: Agent card
nodes.detail: name "Support Ticket Agent" ("(stub)" in stub mode), protocolVersion 0.3.0, url http://localhost:<port>/a2a/json-rpc, capabilities.streaming true, one skill show_tickets.

nodes.label: DefaultRequestHandler
nodes.detail: @a2a-js/sdk 0.3.13 with an InMemoryTaskStore. Calls RestaurantExecutor.execute(requestContext, eventBus) once per incoming message and streams what the executor publishes on the event bus.

nodes.label: execute → run()
nodes.detail: One turn. Publishes the Task (state submitted) if this is a new task; any exception becomes a final failed status with a text part ("The agent could not answer this request: …").

nodes.label: pickA2ui()
nodes.detail: Reads metadata.a2uiClientCapabilities["v0.9"].supportedCatalogIds (or a2uiRendererCapabilities for v1.0; the newest named wins). Unknown versions throw. Result: version profile v0.9 + the ticket catalog id.

nodes.label: readInboundMessage()
nodes.detail: Splits the message into text, action ({ name, context } from data.action with the matching version, or a legacy userAction) and clientError (data.error with string code, surfaceId, message, and path for VALIDATION_FAILED).

nodes.label: System prompt
nodes.detail: createProcessor(profile, catalogIds) builds the processor for the negotiated catalogs (and rejects unknown ones); its promptSnippet holds the catalog document from toJson() and the ticket examples. buildSystemPrompt adds the role and the A2UI format rules.

nodes.label: buildUserQuery()
nodes.detail: Text → the query as is ("Hello!" if empty). open_ticket → fetches the ticket itself with get_tickets and puts it in the query (USER_WANTS_TICKET_DETAILS + TICKET_DATA), saving a model call. resolve_ticket → "User resolved ticket …". Any other action → "User submitted an event: …". The turn is remembered for a possible client retry.

nodes.label: ClientRetries.plan()
nodes.detail: Phase 6, when the message carries a client error. VALIDATION_FAILED with a remembered turn not yet retried → redo that turn once, the first attempt's query starting with the error ("Your previous response was invalid. Validation failed: the renderer reported …"). Otherwise → final input-required status with FALLBACK_TEXT, no model call.

nodes.label: generateUi(): 2 attempts
nodes.detail: MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2. An A2UI problem (A2uiError, or a reply with no A2UI) retries with retryQuery(error); a model or network error (e.g. Gemini 503) retries the original query. Both failing → one text part, FALLBACK_TEXT.

nodes.label: Publish status updates
nodes.detail: status working (no message) when the turn starts; then status working with the A2A parts of each validated, policed batch as it arrives; then the final status: input-required (completed after resolve_ticket), carrying no parts if they were already published.

nodes.label: ModelBackend.streamTurn()
nodes.detail: Gemini in live mode, the stub with STUB_LLM=true. Yields the reply as text chunks.

nodes.label: Gemini chat
nodes.detail: One chat per contextId + version (LRU of 1,000), model gemini-3.6-flash by default, system instruction = the system prompt, one tool (get_tickets), thinking MINIMAL by default. Call 1 usually returns a function call; the tool runs; call 2 streams the A2UI text.

nodes.label: get_tickets
nodes.detail: Filters assets/tickets.json by ticketId, status, priority; count defaults to 8. Returns whole tickets, internal_notes included: keeping them from the browser is the policy's job.
nodes.payload:
[ { "id": "TCK-1042", "title": "Checkout fails with a 502 on card payments", "status": "open",
    "priority": "urgent", "assignee": "Giulia Rossi", "internal_notes": "…", … } ]

nodes.label: StubBackend
nodes.detail: Canned replies: a stub-notice surface plus the example that matches the action (ticket_list, ticket_detail, ticket_resolved), cut into 4 chunks (80-character chunks when leaky). Switches: STUB_INVALID_FIRST, STUB_LEAKY, STUB_CLIENT_INVALID; a query starting "Your previous response was invalid." always gets the valid reply.

nodes.label: stream.feed(chunk) / close()
nodes.detail: @a2ui/agent 0.0.2 Direct JSON stream. Reads <a2ui-json> blocks as they grow and emits a message (again each time it grows) only when a fresh renderer state, built from the negotiated catalogs' Zod, accepts it; a partial one is held back and checked again. A rejected complete message throws A2uiError and ends the attempt.

nodes.label: enforcePolicy()
nodes.detail: Runs on every emitted batch, each re-send included. DEMO_POLICY: forbiddenDataPaths /tickets/*/internal_notes and /ticket/internal_notes, disabledActions delete_ticket. Deletes forbidden data from updateDataModel values; removes components that bind forbidden data or carry a disabled action, mending the tree. Logs one line per strip.

nodes.label: toA2aParts()
nodes.detail: One A2A data part per A2UI message, metadata.mimeType application/a2ui+json; text stays a text part.

paths.label: A prompt turn, live
paths.note: Through the SSR server into the agent and back out as SSE.

paths.label: Server-side retry (stage: invalid priority)
paths.note: STUB_INVALID_FIRST: the agent rejects "critical" before it leaves.

paths.label: Policy on every re-send
paths.note: STUB_LEAKY: notes and Delete never reach the browser.

paths.label: Open a ticket: no tool-decision call
paths.note: open_ticket fetches the ticket before the model is called.

paths.label: VALIDATION_FAILED from the renderer
paths.note: Phase 6: one retry of the last turn, then text.
